subject: Customer ask: NovaBank latency SLA + retention exception - prioritization request
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Customer ask: NovaBank latency SLA + retention exception - prioritization request

Team —

Quick summary: NovaBank (see contacts below) has surfaced two nonstandard requirements as part of the procurement for deal NB-2026-042 that are currently blocking signature:

1) Persistent per-tenant KV-cache pinning / affinity so that certain low-latency trading signals observe ~40% lower median latency on tail-sensitive routes. They describe this as "session-pin" for a high-QPS subset of requests.
2) Audit log retention extension to 24 months (we default to 12) with exportable, immutable format for audits.

Attached are the SOW extract and their SOC2 redline (NovaBank_SOW_asks_v1.pdf; SOC2_redline_NovaBank.docx). Procurement wants a feasibility answer and an ETA on the feature (or documented exception path) within 5 business days — they have a contract review meeting on 2026-03-01.

What I need from product/engineering: can we commit to an MVP plan or an exception path (documented tradeoffs + mitigations) and a rough ETA? If it's a longer-term project, what minimal alternative can we offer now (e.g., dedicated pool + pinned routing + SLA uplift) and what is the incremental cost to the deal?

Karthik — I've cc'd you for the perf numbers you ran last week; Monica — please add customer's timeline if I missed anything.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

---
Attachment(s): NovaBank_SOW_asks_v1.pdf (application/pdf), SOC2_redline_NovaBank.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer ask: NovaBank latency SLA + retention exception - prioritization request

Thanks Rafael — useful summary and attachments. A few clarifying questions from engineering to scope the ask:

- On "KV-cache pinning": do they expect the cache to be pinned to a specific GPU instance pool per tenant, or do they mean sticky placement to ensure hot KV lives in the same serving instance across requests? The implementation and cost differ.
- What are the QPS and concurrency numbers for the subset that needs pinning? Absolute numbers + distribution is critical.
- For retention: do they need full token-level request/response logs or only metadata and request hashes for auditability? Immutable export format (parquet/avro) preference?

If we can't achieve pinning reliably on our current runtime without risking consolidation, an alternative is a dedicated pool with a pinned routing rule and explicit cache warm-up; tradeoffs are higher infra costs and reduced bin-packing. If you can share Karthik's benchmark appendix that shows the 40% number, that will help us evaluate.

Tentative engineering path: 1) quick spike to validate sticky KV with current runtime (2-3 dev days), 2) if feasible, design ~4 week MVP to expose a per-tenant "pin-on-pool" flag + routing policy + documentation; longer if we need kernel/runtime changes.

Happy to run the spike this week if we greenlight it.

- Dev
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer ask: NovaBank latency SLA + retention exception - prioritization request

On Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 01:08 PM Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rafael — useful summary and attachments. A few clarifying questions from engineering to scope the ask:

I've attached the microbenchmark export I ran against their integration environment last week (novabank-bench-2026-02.csv). Key context: their "hot" route is ~6k qps peak during spikes, sustained 800-1,200 qps. The 40% median improvement number comes from a matched test where we kept the same model variant but avoided cross-tenant cache eviction by maintaining a warm KV state on a pinned instance.

Operationally the least-disruptive route for us is: dedicated small pool with explicit tenant affinity, enable KV prefix caching for that pool, and optionally a higher-priority routing lane for that tenant. That gets them ~30-45% tail reductions in our tests. Downside: 2-4x incremental cost on infra for that traffic band and additional operational runbook for cache warming/restarts.

I can share the raw CSV if product/eng want to reproduce the test.

Karthik
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): novabank-bench-2026-02.csv (text/csv)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer ask: NovaBank latency SLA + retention exception - prioritization request

Adding customer timeline: Procurement specifically says contract must be executed by 2026-03-01 or they will reallocate budget to a competitor's pilot. They flagged the KV pinning as a gating technical requirement; retention extension is negotiable but they want the window documented.

If Product can propose a documented exception path (dedicated pool + runbook + elevated cost) that we can include in the SOW, procurement will consider signing with a conditional engineering acceptance. Sales is asking for pricing delta and a short risks note to include in the legal packet.

Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer ask: NovaBank latency SLA + retention exception - prioritization request

Per the spike plan: I can run a 3-day spike starting next Monday to validate sticky KV behavior on a dedicated pool and produce an internal runbook with failure modes. Outcome options: (A) validated + documented exception path (dedicated pool + cost uplift) in ~7 business days; (B) need runtime changes, estimate 6-8 weeks for MVP.

Request to leadership: we need a prioritization decision — can Product allocate a 1-week spike + engineering QA slot if sales commits to a signed conditional SOW that includes a delta MRR to cover infra and eng effort? If leadership prefers not to prioritize, we'll ship (A) as an engineering exception but with no ETA for a native runtime pin feature.

I'll prepare a short risk memo as soon as we confirm direction.

- Dev

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer ask: NovaBank latency SLA + retention exception - prioritization request

Thanks for the clear thread and data. Decision: Product will approve a limited-scope spike now (Dev's 3-day spike) and commit to a 6-week timebox for an MVP if Sales secures a signed conditional SOW that includes a $18,000/month committed uplift to cover dedicated infra + 2 engineer-weeks worth of effort. Conditions:

- The SOW must include a documented exception runbook and an acceptance clause that the feature is "limited-scope" (no SLA beyond documented behaviors).
- Security team to review the SOC2 redline in parallel; if there are additional controls required, we reserve the right to revisit timeline.

Rafael: please confirm you can get Procurement to sign the conditional SOW with the uplift and acceptance language by 2026-02-27 so we can start the spike on 2026-03-02. Dev: please prepare the risk memo and a concise success criteria doc (one page) ahead of the spike.

I'll coordinate with Security for the SOC2 review. If the sales team prefers a different commercial figure, loop Legal early — we negotiated similar arrangements previously and want to avoid last-minute credit asks.

-Marissa
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
